identification.name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Annealed)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely available from aerospace metal distributors as AMS 4928 bar, AMS 4911 sheet/plate, and AMS 4928 billet. Machining requires sharp carbide tooling, low cutting speeds, and flood coolant to manage low thermal conductivity and work-hardening tendency. For metal-AM-printed parts, see the dedicated Titanium Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 (DMLS, Heat Treated) entry in this database rather than this wrought/annealed entry.
identification.notes: Ti-6Al-4V (UNS (Unified Numbering System) R56400, also written Ti 6-4) is the most widely used titanium alloy, accounting for ~50% of global titanium production. Properties given are for the fully annealed condition per AMS (Aerospace Material Specification) 4928. Thermal conductivity is very low (~1/6 that of steel) — this governs machining practice and is a design consideration for heat-dissipating structures. Do not use for sustained structural loads above ~315 °C as strength falls off significantly. Corrosion resistance is excellent in most environments (seawater, acids, body fluids) due to a stable TiO₂ surface layer — avoid contact with liquid oxygen, red fuming nitric acid, and chlorine at elevated temperatures. Biocompatible per ISO (International Organization for Standardization) 5832-3. Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3 = 950/√3 ≈ 549 MPa. Cryogenic thermal conductivity k(T) and coefficient of thermal expansion CTE(T) table data (each as a function of temperature T) are from the NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) Cryogenic Materials Database (nist-cryo-ti64); CTE table values are instantaneous coefficients derived from NIST polynomial fits. Melting point is solidus (1604°C); liquidus 1660°C.

typical_usage: Aerospace primary structures (airframe brackets, engine mounts, fan blades); biomedical implants (orthopaedic stems, bone screws, dental implants); marine hardware and fasteners in salt water; high-performance automotive and motorsport components; chemical processing equipment in corrosive environments; sports equipment (bicycle frames, golf club heads).
